_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Checking the trip request with AirTreks…

description: Submit the customer's trip to AirTreks as a complete, structured trip request - a human travel consultant takes over from there. Ask the traveler for everything before calling, never guess or fill in defaults: name, email, the cities in order (3-letter IATA codes), a departure date for every leg, number of passengers, cabin (economy, premium or business), and their answers to AirTreks' planning questions. Also ask about budget, flexible dates, preferences and anything else the consultant should know. Call once without questionsAnswers to receive the current planning questions to put to the traveler.

agentContext.description: Summary of what the AI agent learned about this trip (auto-generated routing analysis, customer preferences discussed, etc.)

cabin.description: Cabin class (required — ask the customer, there is no default)

cities.description: Ordered list of 3-letter IATA city/airport codes (e.g. ['SFO', 'NRT', 'BKK'])

dates.description: Departure dates, one per leg (ISO format, e.g. '2026-09-15') — a trip with N cities needs N-1 dates, all required. Ask the customer; never invent dates. If they only know roughly, use their stated estimates and set flexibleDates.

name.description: Customer full name (required — the consultant contacts them by name)

notes.description: Additional notes or special requests from the customer

passengers.description: Number of passengers (required — ask the customer, there is no default)

questionsAnswers.description: The customer's answers to AirTreks' planning questions, keyed by question name (e.g. {"guidance": "I want expert guidance from humans"}). The answers must come from the customer — never pick one yourself. A JSON-encoded string of the same object is also accepted. Required, but don't guess the questions: call once without this — the response lists the current questions and their options to ask the customer.

source.description: The AI platform or app this conversation is running in, lowercase (e.g. 'chatgpt', 'claude', 'perplexity'). Only tells AirTreks which channel the request came through — never put customer details here. Omit it if you don't know.

sourceDetail.description: Finer detail on source, such as the app or integration name (e.g. 'trip-pricer'). Never put customer details here.
